An engineer measured two particular features, $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$, for each road bridge in a city. The collected data was stored in a standardized observation matrix, where each row contains both features for a particular bridge.
The first and second principal components of the data are approximately
$v_{1} \approx \begin{bmatrix}0.669 \\ 0.743\end{bmatrix}, v_{2} \approx \begin{bmatrix}0.743 \\ -0.669\end{bmatrix}$.

By combining the two measured features linearly, the engineer wants to construct a single feature that preserves the maximum amount of variance of the collected data. Which of the following could be the best candidate for the new feature?

A scientist measured two particular features, $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$, for each athlete in a team. The collected data was stored in a standardized observation matrix, where each row contains both features for a particular athlete.
The first and second principal components of the data are approximately
$v_{1} \approx \begin{bmatrix}0.894 \\ 0.447\end{bmatrix}, v_{2} \approx \begin{bmatrix}-0.447 \\ 0.894\end{bmatrix}$.

By combining the two measured features linearly, the scientist wants to construct a single feature that preserves the maximum amount of variance of the collected data. Which of the following could be the best candidate for the new feature?

:knowledge-point/title: Representing Principal Components as Linear Combinations
